subject: Critical Thinking
title: Reductio ad Absurdum: Proof by Explosion
description: A micro-lesson that makes Reductio ad Absurdum: Proof by Explosion usable.

hook.text: Assume the opposite of what you want to prove. If it leads to a contradiction, your original claim wins.

buildup.text: This is reductio ad absurdum — reducing an argument to absurdity to disprove it.

discovery.text: Euclid proved there are infinitely many prime numbers this way 2,300 years ago. The proof still stands.

twist.text: It works in everyday arguments too. 'If we never spend money, we'd save everything — but we'd starve.'

climax.text: Reductio is the nuclear option of logic — it destroys positions by showing they self-destruct.

punchline.text: To defeat an idea, follow it to its logical end.

quiz.question: How does reductio ad absurdum work?
options: By assuming the opposite and reaching a contradiction

details.summary: Reductio ad absurdum is a proof strategy that assumes the opposite of what you want to prove and shows that the assumption leads to a contradiction or absurdity. The impossibility of the assumption proves the original claim.
details.whyItMatters: Reductio is one of the most powerful proof techniques in mathematics and philosophy, capable of establishing results no direct argument can.
takeaways: Assume the negation of your conclusion and derive a contradiction
The contradiction proves the original claim must be true
It is used extensively in mathematics and philosophical argument

faq.question: How does reductio ad absurdum work as a proof method?
faq.answer: Assume the opposite of what you want to prove. Show that this assumption logically leads to a contradiction. Since contradictions are impossible, the assumption is false and the original claim is true.

faq.question: What is a famous example of reductio ad absurdum in mathematics?
faq.answer: The proof that the square root of 2 is irrational assumes it is rational, derives a contradiction about shared factors, and concludes the assumption was false.
